blocking_focus: Complete the candidate-bound Tester MCP state matrix.

preservation_constraints.requirement: Keep frozen technical baseline `native_godot_project` passing. Do not treat this as a mandate to preserve the same visible asset, map, HUD family, or material choice if a higher-quality replacement is available and the PRD still fits.

Keep frozen technical baseline `host_godot_boot` passing. Do not treat this as a mandate to preserve the same visible asset, map, HUD family, or material choice if a higher-quality replacement is available and the PRD still fits.

task_specification.objective: Close the three required release-convergence gaps with bounded candidate changes: restore contextual first-run guidance and truthful choice presentation, make dense profiling observable for native qualification, and repair lantern automatic-combat audio causality while preserving the authored map and validated asset bindings.

diagnosis.root_cause: The candidate contains partial guidance, profile, and lantern-audio plumbing, but the first-run presentation remains inactive after deterministic reset, dense profiling still lacks usable native frame-time qualification evidence, and lantern attack/impact events remain unverified on the Effects bus.

stop_conditions: Do not expand into the deferred upgrade-placeholder issue.
Do not replace the preserved authored map or validated weapon assets.
Do not claim formal issue closure or native MCP evidence; Tester and GameLoop Runtime own recapture and verdicts.

strategy.rationale: The required gaps partition into HUD/onboarding, ordinary-release combat/audio integration, and dense-profile qualification. Each task has a bounded implementation surface, while the ordinary-release task also carries the mandatory arena spatial-integrity capability.

code: Run static parse/import checks for all modified GDScript and scene/resource files.
Verify onboarding InputMap bindings, device-generation updates, focus navigation, and retry persistence have no orphaned nodes or stale labels.
Verify lantern audio has one player-report owner, bounded envelopes, distinct semantic stems, and release/reset stop paths.
Verify dense instrumentation is editor/test gated, keeps release defaults disabled, and retains bounded sample history.
runtime: Tester and Runtime recapture deterministic first-run guidance reset, contextual movement/dash/attack/pickup/upgrade prompts, dismissal, Retry persistence, and 1280x720 choice focus states.
Tester and Runtime capture one lantern attack plus quick automatic continuation on Effects, inspect source-event timing and mixed output, then verify release/pause/retry/reset stop behavior.
Tester and Runtime replay ordinary movement through spawn, central landmark, authored streets, collision, external depth, and perimeter/boundary cells to detect disappearance or occlusion.
Tester and Runtime invoke dense prepare/advance/reset and collect native 1920x1080 three-cycle frame-time receipts while preserving host_godot_boot and native_godot_project checks.
visual: Inspect shipped HUD gameplay and upgrade screenshots for visible contextual guidance, bound gameplay illustration, bespoke silhouettes/icons, truthful deltas, and complete focus states.
Inspect ordinary movement/cardinal landmark frames for central-building visibility, external depth, aligned collision, stable perimeter, and absence of disappearance or occlusion.
Inspect adjacent lantern attack frames only as visual corroboration; formal audio causality and performance verdicts remain Tester-owned.

done_when: After deterministic first-run reset and ordinary run start, a visible contextual sequence appears in the real arena with ordinary systems active and teaches movement, dash, automatic attack, pickup collection, and the first upgrade choice.
The sequence uses the bound gameplay illustration, live InputMap/device glyphs, concise action copy, one focused visual at a time, and a discoverable dismiss/recall plus post-dismissal help surface.
Dismissal does not consume combat input, pause the run, reset device context, or replay completed guidance on Retry.

Upgrade choices lead with authored weapon/upgrade silhouettes, compact stat icons, truthful CURRENT-to-new values for at most three decision-relevant deltas, and complete keyboard, mouse, and gamepad focus, hover, unavailable, and selected states.
Tester can retest onboarding visibility/dismissal and the choice hierarchy in one same-session HUD pass.
tasks.instructions: Repair the authoritative run snapshot and HUD presentation so deterministic first-run reset enters a visible, dismissible in-arena teaching path for movement, dash, automatic attacks, pickup collection, and the first upgrade. Bind the existing gameplay illustration to the sequence, derive labels from the authoritative InputMap and active input device, keep the world running, and expose help after dismissal without replaying completed guidance on Retry. Refine the upgrade draft's authored hierarchy with silhouettes/icons, compact stat glyphs, no more than three decision-relevant deltas, truthful current-to-new values, and stable keyboard, mouse, and gamepad focus states. Preserve existing gameplay APIs and validated weapon bindings.
tasks.title: Restore contextual first-run guidance and truthful survivor choices

done_when: A single lantern attack and a cadence-valid quick automatic continuation each produce exactly one short, recognizable semantic transient on the Effects bus.
Source-event timing distinguishes attack onset, miss, concrete hit, metal hit, and character hit; any ringing material cue is bounded and cannot mask the lantern report.
Automatic playback stops on release, pause, Retry, title transition, and lifecycle reset; generic shot VFX never replays the complete player report.

The authored arena is validated at larger traversable scale with an external world/depth treatment, a visible central building/landmark, aligned collision, and no disappearance/occlusion during ordinary movement/movement replay; the playable boundary/perimeter remains explicit and non-passable.
Tester has direct same-session audio and spatial black-box retests plus source-level routing/envelope and collision checks.
tasks.instructions: Trace the lantern's authoritative attack transaction through scripts/audio/mournlight_audio_director.gd, scripts/weapons/warden_lantern_runtime.gd, scripts/combat/attack_runtime.gd, and scenes/audio/mournlight_audio.tscn. Ensure one SEMI-equivalent lantern attack and one cadence-valid quick automatic continuation emit one bounded onset/report and distinct impact semantics on Effects, with independent miss, concrete-hit, metal-hit, and character-hit stems. Shorten or attenuate product-owned ringing material-impact cues; if reliable world-surface tags are absent, disable player world-surface impact audio while preserving impact VFX and character-hit feedback. Preserve the retained authored map and weapon hierarchy. In the same ordinary-release integration pass, expand to a larger traversable scale where needed, retain an external world or external depth, keep the central building or landmark visible, align collision with authored streets, prevent disappearance or occlusion during ordinary movement or movement replay, and enforce the playable boundary or perimeter.
tasks.title: Repair ordinary-release lantern audio and arena spatial integrity

done_when: Dense-profile mode exposes a deterministic test-only profile at the configured 1920x1080 target and records a bounded sample window with frame-time distributions including percentile and maximum values.

Each profile receipt records renderer classification, hardware-qualification eligibility, sample availability, active density, cycle identity, reset isolation, and enough raw samples for native qualification across three retries.
The profile path is editor/test gated, disabled in release defaults, allocation-conscious during normal play, and resets cleanly across restart, death, and lifecycle transitions.
Tester can invoke prepare, advance, and reset independently and inspect candidate-owned receipts/logs without fabricated pass/fail.
tasks.instructions: Extend the existing dense_profile.gd and RunController profile lifecycle rather than adding a second profiler. Make the editor-only dense fixture emit deterministic frame-time, physics-time, render-time, FPS, density, and lifecycle samples plus p50/p95/p99/maximum summaries, explicit renderer/hardware eligibility, sample-availability and reset-isolation receipts, and three-cycle aggregation provenance. Keep qualification gating after sampling so native evidence is not hidden, keep release defaults unchanged, and expose stable prepare/advance/reset controls for Tester.
tasks.title: Make dense profiling natively qualifiable and lifecycle-safe
